title: Shutter Speed Is a Creative Choice, Not a Leftover Setting
excerpt: Most photographers set aperture and ISO first, then let the meter pick the shutter speed. That hands the one setting that decides how motion looks to chance. Decide the motion first, and the rest of the triangle follows.

title: A 5mm Spider, Shot 20 Times Life Size — and Sharp in Every Hair
excerpt: A jumping spider smaller than your fingernail took second place in the Nikon Small World photomicrography competition. At 20x magnification, only a sliver of it can be sharp in one frame, so the photographer stacked dozens of frames into one impossibly sharp portrait.

title: Four Cameras, Seven Lenses — and Every One Earns Its Place
excerpt: A Commonwealth Games photographer carried four bodies and seven lenses to Glasgow and used three most days. The kit is not a shopping list. It is a set of answers to questions asked before the event: how far, how fast, how wide, and what if it rains.
